commits.message:
fix(text): justify pads in the text's base style, as Rich's does (rich-embed-1r2m)

Review pass (medium): setting the table title style as the text's base left
its justify padding unstyled, because RichText padded outside the base.
Rich's Lines.justify pads inside the Text. Markdown's element style moves to
a span under the inline spans, as Rich's is, so a heading's padding stays
plain.

fix(table): a title's end runs on as the text emits it, as Rich's does (rich-embed-1r2m)

Review pass (high): a title or caption with a non-newline end widened its
own row past the table. It is now yielded as the text renders it, the title
style set as the text's base. Pins Rich 9d8f9a3 bytes for that, a progress
description's trailing newline, a standalone leaf's width padding, and
RichText.append leaving the appended text's end behind.

fix(embed)!: a body keeps its own end, as Rich's does (rich-embed-1r2m)

A string reads with Rich's default end, as `render_str` gives it, and a
RichText keeps the end it was given. So `RichText("foo\n")` or "foo\n" in
a table cell, a column, a panel body, a tree label or a layout pane draws
the blank row its newline makes. The sites that set text into a line
clear the end there: print's run and an inline label (panel and rule
titles).

A Layout leaf is now shaped to its region as Rich's `render_lines` shapes
it: each line cropped and padded to the width, and held to the region's
rows.

Expected output is Python Rich 9d8f9a3's, pinned in each renderable's tests.

fix(progress): TimeElapsedColumn and TimeRemainingColumn stop at a task's finish, as Rich's do (rich-progress-jj5r) (#313)

* fix(progress): TimeElapsedColumn and TimeRemainingColumn stop at a task's finish, as Rich's do (rich-progress-jj5r)

A finished task's elapsed clock holds at Task.finishedTime instead of
reading Date.now(); TimeRemainingColumn shows 0:00:00 once finished and
takes elapsedWhenFinished, Rich's elapsed_when_finished. A task never
started shows -:--:-- in the elapsed column, as Rich's does, not 0:00:00.

* fix(progress)!: Progress times tasks on a Clock it is handed, Rich's get_time (rich-progress-jj5r)

Task.started is gone: startTime is undefined until a task starts, and
elapsed is computed once a frame from the clock and handed to every
column, so no column reads a clock. startTask keeps a running task's
start, and TimeRemainingColumn draws a task with no total empty, both as
Rich 9d8f9a3 does.

* fix(progress): TimeRemainingColumn estimates no time until a task has a speed, and rounds up, as Rich does (rich-progress-jj5r)
